openings.claim: Separate lateral registration from downward retention: removable edge stops may resist sliding without corner pressure lifting the opposite corner. Replace seal friction under added corner pressure with two externally clamped strip stops registering perpendicular hatch edges: four strips as two jaw pairs, supplied bolts and rubber pads, drilling only strips. Supplied straps provide modest retention only if reach and attachment suffice; cord tethers removed parts. Remove hatch and projecting jaws for full opening clearance.
openings.discriminator: Rival: tighter straps prevent sliding through friction. Registration predicts reduced sideways displacement at unchanged modest retention; rival improvement depends primarily on increased tension. Persistent opposite-corner lift or card-induced registration loss defeats separation. Compare against stipulated untreated 4 mm displacement; without a matched rival configuration this assesses feasibility, not isolated causation.
openings.probe: First check rim jaw access, strap reach, stop contact height and clearance without seal stress. If constructible within ninety minutes, test one configuration: ten ordinary closure/pull cycles plus two final right-contact-card-disturbed trials, twelve total. Record marked displacement, opposite-corner lift, visible seal damage and single-technician reopening time every trial. Stop on visible damage. Finish observation within twenty minutes; inability to measure stated differences within budget defeats probe feasibility.
openings.uncertainty: Rim geometry and reversible jaw access are unprovided. Strip/bolt rigidity without permanent hatch/rim deformation or excessive pad compression is assumed. Usable strap reach/attachment is unknown; assume no longer strap or new anchor. Stops must engage despite card-induced height change; performance is unestablished.

lineage.reason: Retains causal separation, rival, defeats, constructibility assumptions, stopping and resource limits; declared fit remains uncertain.

decision: Reversible feasibility probe only. Failure of jaw access or strap reach parks fabrication. Preserve existing hatch/rim/seal: no drilling, cutting, gluing or permanent deformation; no powered mechanism; recover loose parts; fully clear marked opening when open. After ten cycles require position within 1 mm, resistance to 20 N and reopening within thirty seconds, with no new visible seal tears. Disturbed closures retain all requirements except seal-contact continuity. Unknown resources authorize no constraint relaxation.
